speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether LTA has plans for a major revamp of bus routes following the staged opening of Thomson-East Coast Line; (b) what is the number of current bus routes with fare revenue (i) exceeding operating cost and (ii) falling behind operating cost; and (c) of these, which are trunk and feeder services respectively in 2019 and 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: When the expansion is completed, our MRT network coverage will be comparable to major cities like New York and London.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Eight in 10 households will be within a 10-minute walk of a train station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Past experience shows that the opening of new rail lines would lead to significant falls in ridership of parallel bus services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: If we keep the services as they are, it will mean more operating subsidies and greater use of public funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The other 345 could not generate enough fare revenues to cover operating costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These are often tough decisions with difficult trade-offs on what we choose to spend on at the national, and also at the local levels and after careful consideration of the impact on different groups of commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We seek the understanding and support of Singaporeans to make such adjustments from time to time, in order to optimise our limited resources to benefit as many commuters as possible.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And the Public Transport Council (PTC) surveys have shown that Singaporeans' satisfaction with the bus service has improved over the years.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Ten years ago, there were subsidies for train services, but they were virtually no subsidies for bus services and yet the two public bus companies at the time were still making slight profit.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Is it just more bus services on the road and more buses on the road?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Speaker, Sir, I would like to thank Mr Ang for highlighting the importance of ensuring financial prudence.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As Mr Ang mentioned, we now spend $1 billion a year in terms of Government subsidies for bus services and another $1 billion a year on train services.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ang asked why is this $1 billion spent or what is it spent on in terms of bus services?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But basically, when you roll out new bus services and that bus service cannot quite cover operating costs – that means the revenue and the fares that are being collected are not enough to cover operating costs and there is a deficit.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And to cover the deficit, we are using the subsidies to pay the operators to run these otherwise non-commercial, sorry, uncommercial, in terms of viability, these bus services would not normally be run.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we understand why these bus services are required.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Sometimes, it is to serve certain areas where we still need to provide the connectivity, but the ridership is low.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Sometimes, it is because there are new housing estates, new residents and we do need to provide new services to connect them to key transport nodes like MRT stations and bus interchanges.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, in the process of doing so, we cannot keep on increasing the total sum of subsidies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because if we do that, the fiscal burden for this generation and future generations of Singaporeans will increase.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, our approach is as far as possible, we want to be able to meet new demand, cater to new groups of commuters, new services, by re-adjusting some of the existing services that have low ridership.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And as I mentioned earlier in my main reply, an example of these services will include those that run parallel to the train lines.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In fact, one of the concepts that I think we need to get people used to, is that what we want is to provide adequate transport connectivity via public transport through a combination of bus and MRT.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This means that we want to ensure that residents have adequate connectivity between their homes and the train station with buses increasingly focusing on the first and last mile connectivity, to complement the expanding MRT network that will provide the connectivity for longer travel distances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may just make a request, I wonder if LTA will consider implementing surveys to consider continuing to ply certain popular routes at a reduced frequency, perhaps during off-peak hours, and even if at a loss?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And especially if these routes prove popular with the elderly, who tend to prefer bus services as opposed to MRTs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is, he said that even if the bus services were to lose money, will we still be willing to provide?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Actually, we have been doing so for the large majority of bus services.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If you are talking about new services, we want to have more new services, it is not that we cannot do it but we have to assess this carefully, because resources are finite and we need to ensure financial prudence.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, if we spend on one, we will have less resources to spend on another.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we are going to cater to new demand and yet, we do not wish to take away or adjust existing bus routes, then you can work out the sums.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are all important objectives and ideally, we want to be able to do all of them.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, therefore, we need to continually review how we can optimise the use of our scarce resources.
